title: What is Wrong with Perplexity for Long-context Language Modeling?

contributions.purpose: Explain why perplexity (PPL) fails to reflect LLMs' long-context abilities.
contributions.mechanism: Fine-grained analysis of the role of individual tokens; introduce Long-Short Difference (LSD), a causal intervention on context length (log-prob under long vs. truncated short context) to identify 'key tokens' that gain from long context.
contributions.evaluation: PPL on answer tokens strongly correlates with LongEval accuracy while PPL on non-answer tokens shows almost no correlation; LSD-based key-token identification matches LongEval answer tokens with up to 98.2% accuracy.
contributions.source_quote: We find that PPL overlooks key tokens, which are essential for long-context understanding, by averaging across all tokens and thereby obscuring the true performance of models in long-context scenarios.

contributions.purpose: Provide a reliable, unsupervised metric for evaluating LLMs' long-context capabilities on natural corpora.
contributions.mechanism: LongPPL (Long-context Perplexity): compute perplexity averaged only over the LSD-selected key tokens.
contributions.evaluation: Across diverse LLMs and long-context benchmarks, LongPPL strongly correlates with benchmark scores, e.g., Pearson correlation of -0.96 on GovReport vs LongBench, vs near-zero (-0.18) for standard PPL.
contributions.source_quote: we propose LongPPL, a novel metric that focuses on key tokens by employing a long-short context contrastive method to identify them.

contributions.purpose: Improve long-context fine-tuning by prioritizing tokens that gain most from long context.
contributions.mechanism: LongCE (Long-context Cross-Entropy) loss: a re-weighting strategy that upweights key tokens, estimated by the model itself, alternating between estimating and optimizing key tokens (plug-and-play).
contributions.evaluation: Consistent improvements over conventional CE across multiple LLMs and benchmarks, with a maximum accuracy gain of 22% on LongEval.
contributions.source_quote: we introduce LongCE (Long-context Cross-Entropy) loss, a re-weighting strategy for fine-tuning that prioritizes key tokens, leading to consistent improvements across diverse benchmarks.

self_declared_provenance.quote: recent studies have challenged this common practice by revealing a huge discrepancy between perplexity and actual performance on long-context tasks (Hu et al., 2024a; Hsieh et al., 2024).

From a causal perspective, s_i serves as the counterfactual context created by the intervention (dropping long context), and the LSD estimates the individual treatment effect (ITE) (Hernan & Robins, 2010) of long context using the language model.

notes: All results positive (strong correlations, consistent gains). ICLR 2025 accept. Code released. No negative/tie results highlighted beyond the intended negative finding that standard PPL is uncorrelated with long-context performance.
